status: Phase 1: extractor pins, stored per-frame keypoints, and normalization step 1 (aspect + shoulders). Phase 2 adds the rest of normalization.

stored.description: What the offline extractor (Python) and the live extractor (browser) both produce per frame, before normalization.
stored.coordinates: MediaPipe normalized image coordinates of the UNMIRRORED frame: x in [0,1] of width (to the right), y in [0,1] of height (down), z as MediaPipe reports it.

pose.note: Upper body = MediaPipe pose landmarks 0-24 (face points, arms, hand stubs, hips). Legs 25-32 are dropped. left/right = the signer's own side.

hands.order: MediaPipe hand landmark order (0 = wrist ... 20 = pinky tip)
hands.sides: left/right = the signer's own hand (measured 99% agreement with pose wrists 15/16 on unmirrored frames, ADR 002)

stored.missing: A missing pose or hand is stored as zeros with its *_present flag false. Never NaN.
stored.timestamps: t_ms: int64 milliseconds from the decoder's presentation timestamps, strictly increasing.
stored.frame_size: (width, height) of the image MediaPipe actually processed (after any downscaling; never the container's claim). Chrome on macOS may process 1920x1088 for 1080p video.

step1_aspect.description: Convert MediaPipe normalized coords to frame-height units using frame_size: x' = x*W/H, y' = y, z' = z*W/H (z uses roughly x's scale, per MediaPipe docs).
step1_aspect.use_frame_size: the size of the image passed to MediaPipe (videoWidth/videoHeight of the actual frame in the browser)

step2_body.description: Subtract the shoulder midpoint and divide by shoulder width, both in aspect-correct units.
invariants_tested: same body at 16:9, 4:3, 854x480 and padded 1920x1088 gives identical features

resample.times: T evenly spaced times from the first to the last timestamp
resample.interp: linear if the part is present in both neighbours, else nearest frame

velocity.definition: difference of the 190 coordinate features between consecutive resampled frames; zero where the part is missing at either end; first frame zero

downscale.description: Frames are downscaled to `height` rows before MediaPipe, offline and live (ADR 007). Never upscaled.
downscale.width_rule: keep aspect; width = 2 * floor(W * height / H / 2 + 0.5) (even, halves round UP in both Python and TypeScript)
downscale.browser_choice_evidence: reports/phase1_browser_downscale.json: pixel MAE 0.29 vs INTER_AREA in Chromium and Chrome; canvas paths differ between browsers
